title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.03044v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate human opinions, but prior work reports conflicting results: some studies find promising alignment with human survey data, while others find persona collapse and weak demographic sensitivity. We propose that much of this conflict stems from conflating two distinct tasks. We call the first task emulation, in which models generate individual responses that aggregate into a population distribution. We call the second task estimation, in which models directly predict the population distribution. Evaluating six matched base and post-trained models on the Pew American Trends Panel, we find that base models are the stronger emulators: they produce response distributions closer to human ground truth and better preserve demographic structure. translated_title: 模拟还是估计？基础模型与后训练语言模型在观点模拟中的差异化优势
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型越来越多地被用于模拟人类观点，但先前的研究报告了相互矛盾的结果：一些研究发现模型与人类调查数据具有良好的一致性，而另一些研究则发现存在角色坍塌和对人口统计特征敏感性弱的问题。我们提出，这种矛盾在很大程度上源于混淆了两种不同的任务。我们将第一种任务称为“模拟”，即模型生成个体响应，再将其聚合为总体分布；我们将第二种任务称为“估计”，即模型直接预测总体分布。通过在Pew American Trends Panel数据集上评估六个相互匹配的基础模型和后训练模型，我们发现基础模型是更强的模拟器：它们生成的响应分布更接近人类真实数据，并能更好地保留人口统计结构。而后训练模型通常是更强的估计器，在被直接询问时能够产生更准确的分布预测。我们认为……
tldr: 本文提出区分“模拟”（生成个体响应后聚合为总体分布）与“估计”（直接预测总体分布）两种任务，发现基础模型更擅长模拟人类观点分布，而后训练模型更擅长直接估计总体分布。
en_tdlr: This paper distinguishes between "emulation" (generating individual responses that aggregate into population distributions) and "estimation" (directly predicting population distributions), finding that base models are stronger emulators of human opinion distributions, while post-trained models are stronger estimators of them.
